Valid, fixed in e4b6ea149d.

A polling start line is now dropped only when its own successful end follows it. Starts and ends are paired in order, by command, request ID and client ID, because some clients reuse request IDs (for example `hub-client-1`). As a result:

- A poll that never finished keeps its start line, so a hub that stopped answering still shows up in the report.
- A failed poll keeps both its start and its end.

Added a test for a start with no end, and tightened the existing test to check that a failed poll keeps both lines.

Valid, fixed in b49479af3d.

The fallback now only picks an app that is still connected **and** still attached to the task: `sessionState.participants`, which `session.detach` and unregister already maintain. An app that detached is skipped, so the request goes to one that can still answer. If none is left, it fails right away instead of waiting.

The hub test now covers your scenario: owner, detached app and joined app, in that order. Against the previous code it picks the detached app; with the fix it picks the joined one. I also re-ran the end-to-end handoff: after the owner leaves, the joined app keeps the task running.

Fixed in 0b6e96f80b. `factsOf` now reads only the messages after the newest real prompt (a user message whose `userRunSpan` isn't 0), so an earlier turn's edits or errors no longer drive Verify, Review or Fix; reminders, hook context and steering that core injects mid-run carry `userRunSpan: 0` and stay inside the turn.

Fixed in 85ba54c1e8. When a Skip names a row that sits before the cursor (one New set already paged past), the cursor now moves back by one. Only the skipped row leaves the pool, and the rows on screen stay put. A test pins your sequence: New set, then a late Skip for Verify, leaves Review/Wrap up/Next step in view, and Undo skip brings Verify back to the front. I also fuzzed 4,000 random verb sequences offline against "a skip hides only its row, more drops only the last row, Undo skip brings its row into view". The fuzzer finds this bug without the fix and finds nothing with it.

Fixed in 202642e: parseStatus now keeps the original path on R/C records (originalPath on the file entry). The webview includes it in unstage actions (unstagePaths helper, used for row, group, and breadcrumb unstage) and passes it to get_git_file_diff so a staged rename reads HEAD at the old path. Covered by a real-repo test that git mv's a file, checks the diff shows the old contents, unstages both paths, and verifies the old path is no longer staged as a deletion.
